derMessages.title: <rule name> must be on the last line of a subderivation
derMessages.text:
You appear to be attempting to Box and Cancel on a line that has other lines from the same subderivation below it. You may Box and Cancel only in the bottom line of a subderivation. This subderivation contains <branch lines left> below the present line.

You may wish to delete <branch lines left> or the present line using the Alt+Delete key combination. 

To recreate the present line at the bottom of the subderivation, add a new, empty line as follows: First verify that that the subderivation is not already boxed. If it is, Unbox using Ctrl+Shift+X. Then place the cursor in the present bottom line of the subderivation, and press Alt+Enter. (In Command Mode, Alt+Enter produces a new line without executing any command.)

derMessages.title: lines not negations of each other
derMessages.text:
You appear to be attempting to justify a Box and Cancel step by ID (Indirect Derivation). However, neither of the referenced lines: 
<indent 5><stack 1> 
<indent 5><stack 2> 
is the exact negation of the other. 

Remember, a formula such as
<indent 5>\l~P->Q, 
is short for 
<indent 5>(~P->Q), 
rather than
<indent 5>~(P->Q)
Hence, it is not the negation of 
<indent 5>P->Q,

derMessages.title: not subordinate to any show line
derMessages.text:
This message is posted for lines that are not subordinate to any Show line, and are not themselves Show lines.  Note that the reverse highlight, which appears when your cursor is in the line, appears on the Problem Line, and not on any Show line within the derivation.  

Lines that are not subordinate to any Show line will, of course, never be boxed, and lines that are not Show lines will never contain canceled Show.  Thus the lines flagged by this message will prevent the derivation from ever being technically "complete", i.e. from ever being one in which every line is either in a box or contains a canceled "Show".  The importance of a derivation being complete first appears in Chapter 3, wherein it is possible to give a derivation, albeit incomplete, for a fallacious argument.  

Lines for which this message is posted should either be deleted (Alt+Delete), indented (Alt+[Right Arrow]), or become Show lines (Ctrl+Shift+S).

This message is posted for lines that are not subordinate to any Show line, and are not themselves Show lines.  Note that the reverse highlight, which appears when your cursor is in the line, appears on the Problem Line, and not on any Show line within the derivation.  

Lines that are not subordinate to any Show line will, of course, never be boxed, and lines that are not Show lines will never contain canceled Show.  Thus the lines flagged by this message will prevent the derivation from ever being technically "complete", i.e. from ever being one in which every line is either in a box or contains a canceled "Show".  The importance of a derivation being complete first appears in Chapter 3, wherein it is possible to give a derivation, albeit incomplete, for a fallacious argument.  

Lines for which this message is posted should either be deleted (Alt+Delete), indented (Alt+[Right Arrow]), or become Show lines (Ctrl+Shift+S).

derMessages.title: improper substitution
derMessages.text:
It appears that you are attempting to apply the rule <rule name>.  However, the substitution you propose will cause a clash of variables.  

Either, there is a free occurrence of <arg 1> in <stack 1> which would be picked up by the quantifier phrase <operator><arg 1>, or <stack 1> already contains an internal quantifier on <arg 1> that will capture the new occurrences of <arg 1>.  

In answer to the request to specify a variable of generalization, you must specify a variable that is not free in <stack 1>, and that will not be captured by an existing quantifier in <stack 1>.

derMessages.title: <text>
derMessages.text:
This explanation is intended to serve for many different messages.

Messages of the form "can not map xxx to yyy" indicate that the substitution you proposed in answer to a query was of the wrong grammatical type.  For example, if you answered a query for an instantial term with "P", such a message would be generated because "P" is a sentence letter and not a term.  Similarly, if you were introducing an instance of a theorem, and answered a query for a substitution instance of "Q" with "x", the message "can not map Q to x" would be generated because "x" is a variable, and cannot replace a sentence letter.

Messages of the form "parse error at token n" indicate that the expression in the WFF field is not well-formed.  The parser believes that the first error occurs at about the nth symbol.

Messages of the form "lexical error at token n" indicate that the expression in the WFF field contains a symbol that is not in the vocabulary of the language.  The parser believes that the first such occurs at about the nth symbol.

If there is something in the Justification field, and Command Mode is enabled, you may regard the justification as a command, and attempt to execute it by placing the cursor in the Justification field, and pressing Shift+Enter.  The command will then be executed, or, if there is an error in the justification, a different message will appear.

<indent 3><gen all>

free occurrence of "<gen var>" that was free in 
<indent 5><inst wff>

symMessages.title: SymNot007
symMessages.text:
You create an Answer by working the problem and then clicking Add in
the Answer Manager. You can use the Direct entry button to quickly
create an answer, which will appear in the workspace (with empty text
boxes), from which you can use Answer/Add to add it to the list of
answers. You can add as many Answers as you wish, either right from
the workspace or starting out from the Direct entry facility.

To be added to the Answer list, every branch of the workspace answer
must terminate in an Atomic expression.

If you wish to edit one of the Answers in the list, perhaps to fill
in or change what is in the text boxes, click on the Answer to select
it, and click Enter to put it into the workspace. Edit it in the
workspace. When you are finished editing it, reopen the Answer
Manager, select the Answer and click Replace to replace the original
answer with the edited answer. You can also use Delete to remove any
Answer in the list.

Be sure to fill in the text boxes of your favorite answer(s) if you
wish the Hint facility to be able to offer fully explanatory hints.
If you wish to suppress Hints for certain Instructor Problems, use
only the 800 versions of those problem in your Assignments.

Only Problems with at least one Answer can be Uploaded.

symMessages.title: SymNot008
symMessages.text:
Use this dialog to create a Scheme of Abbreviation.

Schemes of Abbreviation are presented using Placeholders, {1}, {2},
{3}, ... instead of variables or other symbolic terms. The
placeholders are entered by using the keyboard combinations Alt+1,
Alt+2, Alt+3, ... Enter the Predicate or Term Letter on the left
followed by the appropriate number of distinct placeholders (with or
without parentheses as required by the syntax). On the right, enter
the corresponding English (plus placeholders) expression.  The Tab
key moves you back and forth between columns.
